pr_title: fix: dont overflow when calculating date range over very long periods

issue_context.title: Unable to create date ranges for very large time periods(>=0.19.13)
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

pl.date_range(pl.date(1900, 1, 1), pl.date(2300, 1, 1), eager=True)
```


### Log output

```shell
no output
```


### Issue description

When executed, it does nothing and the program stops working.
In (<=0.19.12), it worked fine.

comments:
Can reproduce. It tries to use up all my RAM.

With that start date, this is the last end date that works for me:
```python
>>> pl.date_range(pl.date(1900, 1, 1), pl.date(2192, 4, 10), eager=True)
shape: (320_255,)
```

While debugging this, I've also noticed that `date_range` appears to panic with invalid dates:
```python
>>> pl.date_range(pl.date(1900, 1, 1), pl.date(1900, 2, 300), eager=True)
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at crates/polars-plan/src/dsl/function_expr/range/utils.rs:9:10:
PanicException: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
```
(Not sure if this needs a separate issue to be opened.)

If you run this example in debug build, you can fire an overflow here:
https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/38b532211e0ffbc5a152c756b3bd0a9d93d5bf01/crates/polars-time/src/windows/duration.rs#L710

In release build, it will be wrapped then. We changed the start point in #12317, maybe @MarcoGorelli has more ideas.
thanks for the report - maybe #12317 needs reverting I'm afraid. If anyone needs the last day of the month, they can do `.dt.month_end()`, trying to "do the right" is just going to mess things up
thanks @phi-friday for the excellent bug report

review_comments: this could be cleaner with, say, `MS_WEEK` and `US_WEEK`...but this simple change at least fixes the issue
